metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent low points or sentiment-neutral periods.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days, particularly when sentiment is flat or neutral.
- After a sharp price spike, model overestimates continuation, leading to overshoots in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias, pulling prices back toward prior averages instead of capturing momentum.
- In the absence of sentiment signals, model should not assume trend continuation; instead, treat as stationary or mean-reverting until sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model should not ignore it — even with neutral sentiment, momentum may persist.
- If true outcome shows a sharp reversal or drop after a spike, model should adjust downward by 1–2 days in forecast, especially if sentiment remains flat.
- When true price exceeds forecast by >10% in early days of forecast horizon, model should reduce subsequent forecast values by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
